back: The distance of open water over which the wind blows; a longer fetch gives bigger waves.
Constructive: low, about 6–8 per minute, strong swash, build the beach. Destructive: high, about 10–14 per minute, strong backwash, remove sediment.
The movement of sediment along the coast in a zig-zag path: swash carries material up the beach at an angle and backwash returns it straight down.
Hydraulic action, cavitation, abrasion (corrasion), attrition and solution.
Waves slow in shallow water off a headland and bend, concentrating energy on the headland and spreading it in the bay.
A stretch of coast, with inputs, stores, transfers and outputs of sediment, in which the movement of sediment is largely self-contained.
Wavelength L ≈ 1.56 T² (m); speed c = L ÷ T ≈ 1.56 T (m/s); waves per minute = 60 ÷ T; energy ∝ height².
Inputs (cliffs, rivers, sea floor, drift in) minus outputs (drift out, offshore loss, dredging): a surplus builds the coast; a deficit lets it retreat.

front: Ways in which waves transport sediment
back: Traction (rolling), saltation (bouncing), suspension (carried within the water) and solution (dissolved).
